scientific_question: Can the length-versus-screening response-direction contrast be retained after a material nonseparable mode coupling removes the rectangle's one-field spectral-demixing loophole?

problem.domain: A strip with normalized propagation coordinate xi in (0,1) and periodic transverse coordinate y in (0,2 pi).
problem.equation: After cosine Galerkin projection, u_xixi = a^2[-u_yy + lambda^2 u + 5 q(xi,y) u].
problem.coefficient: q=exp(log(0.8)+sin(2 pi xi+0.3) cos(y)+0.45 sin(4 pi xi-0.8) cos(2y)+0.25 sin(2 pi xi+1.2) cos(3y)).
problem.boundary_contract: Eight independent cosine coefficients at the left boundary; zero Dirichlet data at the right boundary.
problem.source_P: Same uniform screening as target; increase propagation length until the exact relative response distance is 15%.
problem.source_G: Same propagation length as target; increase uniform screening until the exact relative response distance is 15%.
problem.drive_distribution: Independent zero-mean coefficients with variance inversely proportional to each target response column's energy, normalized to mean variance one.

registered_gates.material_nonseparability: The best response obtained by retaining only same-index input/output mode pairs has at least 4% relative root-mean-square error under the declared drive distribution.
registered_gates.causal_separation: The exact source-response displacement angle is at least 30 degrees.
registered_gates.spectral_crossover: Source P is closer on at least three of the four lowest input modes, and source G is closer on at least three of the four highest modes.
registered_gates.nonextreme_drive_distribution: The largest prescribed drive variance is at most five times the smallest.
registered_gates.source_distance_control: Both reference-resolution source radii equal 15% within 1e-7 absolute.
registered_gates.boundary_certification: The left-boundary response equals identity and the right-boundary response equals zero to 1e-9 maximum absolute error.
registered_gates.resolution_stability: Medium versus reference changes the response angle by at most 2 degrees and the diagonal-demixing error by at most 0.5 percentage points; both medium source radii remain within 0.3 percentage points of 15%; the low/high source winner pattern is identical.

decision_rule: Advance only to an empirical target-only saturation pilot if every gate passes. Failure rejects this coefficient profile as a transfer instrument; it does not refute response-direction reuse.
scope: This is a causal instrument inside one coercive elliptic propagation class, not a general geometry-transfer result.
Passing removes the known separable-demixing defect but does not prove a lower bound on target simulations; the target-only learning curve must still be measured.
No architecture comparison or transfer outcome is part of this formal gate.
